papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and machine learning analyses to identify a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), revealing potential therapeutic targets. The findings link TDT-related molecular features to patient outcomes, offering a new tool for risk stratification and treatment guidance.

papers.title: Deciphering lung cancer at high resolution: a narrative review of applications of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics sequencing.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Many patients are still facing limited treatment benefit or therapeutic resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution characterization of cellular states, whereas spatial transcriptomics (ST) preserves tissue architecture and maps gene expression within the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review summarizes recent advances in scRNA-seq and ST in lung cancer and discusses how these technologies have improved our understanding of tumor biology and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have advanced our understanding of lung cancer biology, including tumor heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment. It highlights how these high-resolution technologies can inform therapeutic response and resistance, offering a comprehensive overview of recent applications in the field.

papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to its PDZ domain. Using advanced computational modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics, we identified a selective and specific small molecule inhibitor of GIPC1 (GIPCi) targeting its PDZ doma
papers.summary: This study uses AI-driven computational modeling and machine learning to identify a small molecule inhibitor (GIPCi) that targets the PDZ domain of GIPC1, a scaffolding protein overexpressed in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The inhibitor shows selective and specific activity, potentially overcoming the previous 'undruggable' status of GIPC1 and offering a new therapeutic avenue for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Unraveling the roles of DKK1 and S100P in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: Insights from machine learning, single-cell/spatial transcriptomics, and functional validation.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with a 5-year survival rate of only 13%. Despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, the prognosis of PDAC remains poor, largely owing to its complex tumor microenvironment, epithelial heterogeneity, and therapeutic resistance. In this study, we integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics (ST), machine learning analysis, and functional validation to investigate candidate biomarkers associated with PDAC progression. By intersecting genes selected using L
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify DKK1 and S100P as potential biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Functional validation suggests these genes may play roles in PDAC progression, offering new insights into the disease's tumor microenvironment and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: SPAE: Deciphering Cell Cycle Dynamics and Cell States in Single-cell RNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology have enabled the investigation of gene expression changes at the single-cell level, particularly for elucidating the heterogeneity among cells and complex biological processes. This technique reveals subtle molecular differences within individual cells, thereby offering a unique viewpoint for the investigation of cell cycle progression, cellular differentiation, and disease pathogenesis. However, accurately identifying and analyzing cell cycle dynamics in scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of the data and
papers.summary: The paper introduces SPAE, a new computational method for deciphering cell cycle dynamics and cell states from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying cell cycle phases in complex scRNA-seq datasets, providing a tool to better understand cellular heterogeneity and biological processes.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects panels of marker genes for cell types by framing the problem as a minimal set-covering optimization, rather than relying on one-gene-at-a-time differential expression. Applied to neocortical neural stem cell data, it identifies gene panels that better capture developmental progression and cell identity. This approach improves marker gene selection for single-cell RNA-seq analysis by considering gene redundancy and complementarity.

papers.title: An Integrated Transcriptional and Post-Transcriptional Regulatory Circuit Orchestrated by NUDT21 Maintains the Proliferation and Survival of Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor, associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21 as a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation in neuroblastoma, revealing an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that maintains tumor cell proliferation and survival. The findings highlight a previously unexplored role for APA in neuroblastoma and suggest NUDT21 as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a versatile transcriptomic aging clock that accurately predicts biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework, Pasta maps chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation, offering a broadly applicable tool for aging research.

papers.title: Loom: Multi-Region Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomics with Local Neighborhoods and Global Trajectories.
papers.abstract: We present Loom, a spatial transcriptomics (ST) visual computing system to support the analysis of pseudo-temporal trajectories, comparative investigation across samples and regions of interest, and the examination of spatially structured processes within local microenvironments. ST is a molecular profiling technology that measures gene expression directly within a thin tissue section while preserving its spatial organization. For practical application-driven analyses, the ST local microenvironment data needs to be integrated with cell reference datasets and temporal simulations of cell behavi
papers.summary: Loom is a new visual computing system for spatial transcriptomics that integrates local neighborhood analysis with global pseudo-temporal trajectories, enabling comparative investigation across samples and regions of interest. It supports the examination of spatially structured processes within local microenvironments, addressing practical needs in ST data analysis.

papers.title: An automated platform for spatial functional modeling and fingerprint analysis of tissue molecular landscapes.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables high-resolution molecular profiling while preserving tissue architecture, creating new opportunities to investigate how disease-associated pathways are organized within tissues. However, existing analytical approaches largely focus on individual pathways or cell types and do not provide a unified framework for modeling spatially varying pathway interactions across tissue sections and anatomical planes. We present an integrative framework, Spatial Fingerprints Analytics (SFinx), that introduces the concept of a spatial fingerprint for representing patterns o
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces SFinx, an automated platform that models spatial molecular landscapes by generating 'spatial fingerprints'—unified representations of how pathway interactions vary across tissue sections. It provides a framework for integrative analysis of spatial transcriptomics data beyond individual pathways or cell types, enabling comparative studies across tissue sections and anatomical planes.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology technologies, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are advancing the study of cancer epigenetics by preserving tissue architecture and revealing how epigenetic regulation varies across tumor microenvironments. It highlights the limitations of bulk and single-cell methods that lose spatial context and emphasizes the potential of integrating spatial omics to understand tumor heterogeneity and cell communication.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study presents a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye, overcoming the technical challenge of melanin interference by using a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method compatible with immunohistochemistry. The authors generated a comprehensive atlas of pigmented tissue development and integrated it with re-analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data, providing a valuable resource for understanding eye development.

papers.title: A multimodal interrogation of Broca's area in the pediatric and adult human brain.
papers.abstract: Language is a defining trait of our species, and disruptions in language acquisition can have profound consequences to the individuals affected. Uncovering the neurodevelopmental basis of this complex trait requires detailed molecular and cellular insights into the neocortical areas that support linguistic abilities. Here we performed joint gene expression and chromatin accessibility profiling at single-nucleus resolution (10x Genomics Single cell Multiome) and spatial transcriptomic profiling (Xenium high-plex in situ spatial transcriptomics) of Broca's area alongside adjacent motor cortical
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint provides a multimodal, single-cell and spatial atlas of Broca's area in the developing and adult human brain, integrating gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics to reveal the molecular and cellular architecture underlying language-related cortical areas. The findings offer new insights into the neurodevelopmental basis of language and provide a valuable resource for studying language-related disorders.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This paper introduces a contextual activity score (CAS) to infer ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data, overcoming limitations of the standard Alu Editing Index (AEI) which requires raw sequencing reads and is unsuitable for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. The CAS framework enables estimation of ADAR activity across diverse transcriptomic technologies, potentially benefiting studies of neural function, immune regulation, and cancer.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), revealing a shared reservoir of transcriptome-derived neoantigens that could be targeted for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that these neoTSTs may offer a broader and more common source of immunogenic targets than mutation-derived neoantigens, potentially improving vaccine design for HCC patients.

papers.title: Organism-scale annotation with Pan-human Azimuth.
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases now span many human tissues, but inconsistent annotations across studies limit their utility as a unified reference. We introduce Pan-human Azimuth, a supervised neural network that maps human cells from diverse tissues and datasets onto a single hierarchical organism-scale typology. Developed through NIH HuBMAP, the model is trained on a uniquely curated corpus designed to maximize diversity across tissues and technologies while enforcing uniform, interpretable annotations and stringent quality control. The use of a single organism-wide reference enables us to map tens of
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Pan-human Azimuth is a supervised neural network that maps human cells from diverse tissues and datasets onto a single hierarchical organism-scale typology, addressing the issue of inconsistent annotations across single-cell atlases. Trained on a curated corpus from the NIH HuBMAP, it provides uniform, interpretable annotations and stringent quality control, enabling mapping of tens of thousands of cells across tissues and technologies.

papers.title: Human Myometrial Cell Fate under Chronic Oxidative Stress for Leiomyomagenesis.
papers.abstract: Uterine Leiomyoma are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age. Studies show that both leiomyoma and surrounding myometrium exist in a state of high oxidative stress, characterized by reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and impaired antioxidant defenses including defects of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD). Oxidative stress has been proposed as a driver of leiomyoma initiation by promoting oxidative DNA damage leading to mutations in MED12 and leiomyoma growth. We hypothesize that chronic oxidative stress in human myometrial cells induces cellular remodeling and ge
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how chronic oxidative stress affects human myometrial cells, potentially driving the initiation of uterine leiomyomas (fibroids). The authors hypothesize that oxidative stress causes cellular remodeling and genetic changes, such as mutations in the MED12 gene, which are commonly found in leiomyomas. The study aims to clarify the mechanistic link between oxidative stress and leiomyomagenesis, offering potential insights into prevention or treatment.

papers.title: Autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus: insights from integrative multi-omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the emergence of autoantibodies and deposition of immune complexes. SLE presents with heterogeneous multi-organ involvement that varies among patients and its mechanisms have been investigated to facilitate appropriate stratification and treatment selection. Bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq have provided important insights into the pathogenesis of SLE; however, these approaches are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined cell subsets and known markers, which can introduce bias and restrict their ability to fu
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrative multi-omics analyses, particularly single-cell approaches, are advancing our understanding of autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). It highlights the limitations of bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq in capturing cellular heterogeneity and emphasizes the potential of single-cell technologies to reveal disease mechanisms and improve patient stratification.

papers.title: Robust and generalizable CNV detection for single-cell sequencing assays.
papers.abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) are genomic structural variants that are strongly linked to cancer progression and genetic disorders. CNVs can be highly heterogeneous at population and tissue scale; thus, single-cell resolution detection holds great promise for studying clonal evolution and CNV-driven changes. Despite advanced sc-RNA-seq CNV detection methods, accurate methods for epigenomic single-cell modalities lag behind. We developed RIDDLER; a robust, unsupervised method that uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to detect CNVs across multiple single-cell modalities and assays. RIDDLER u
papers.summary: This paper introduces RIDDLER, a robust and unsupervised computational method for detecting copy number variations (CNVs) from single-cell sequencing data, with a focus on epigenomic modalities like sc-ATAC-seq. RIDDLER uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to improve accuracy and generalizability across different single-cell assays, addressing a key gap in CNV detection for non-transcriptomic data.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal mechanistic insights of FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of renal malignancy, characterized by extensive vascularization and poor prognosis. Early detection markedly improves patient outcomes, and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA, encoded by FOLH1) imaging has recently emerged as a valuable diagnostic tool for ccRCC. However, the cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic contribution of FOLH1 expression within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to characterize FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), revealing their cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic roles in the tumor microenvironment. The findings provide new insights into how these cells may contribute to tumor vascularization and progression, with potential implications for PSMA-based diagnostics and therapies.

papers.title: Scalable hypothalamic neuron differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells suitable for modeling metabolic disorders.
papers.abstract: The hypothalamus, composed of multiple nuclei, is essential for maintaining the body's homeostasis. Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains key neuronal populations, including appetite-suppressing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons that regulate energy and glucose balance. Here, we present a chemically defined, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, compatible with robotic cell culture platforms for high-throughput use. Neuronal identity was validated by MERFISH single-cell tran
papers.summary: This paper presents a scalable, chemically defined method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, which are key regulators of energy and glucose balance. The method is compatible with robotic cell culture platforms, enabling high-throughput studies, and neuronal identity was validated using MERFISH single-cell transcriptomics. This resource could facilitate modeling of metabolic disorders and drug screening.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics characterize CD8+ exhausted T cells in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer resists immunotherapy due to a suppressive immune microenvironment where CD8+ T cells play a key role. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, we characterized CD8+ exhausted T (Tex) cells in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We generated single-cell profiles from PDAC tumors and matched peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and performed T cell sub-analysis. We found CXCL13 upregulated and GZMK downregulated in CD8+ Tex cells. Cell-cell interaction analysis showed that T cells most frequently interacted with myeloid cells and cancer cells via ligan
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics to characterize CD8+ exhausted T (Tex) cells in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), identifying CXCL13 upregulation and GZMK downregulation in these cells. Cell-cell interaction analysis reveals that T cells most frequently interact with myeloid cells and cancer cells, providing insights into the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that may inform immunotherapies.

papers.title: Myasthenia thymus reprograms class-switched B cells into BAFF-dependent survivors.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) presents a clinical challenge where autoantibody titers poorly predict disease severity, and thymectomy provides inconsistent benefits. We hypothesized that thymic B cells acquire survival mechanisms that bypass canonical tolerance checkpoints, enabling persistence independent of antigen-specific selection. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, V(D)J repertoire analysis, and spatial transcriptomics to generate the largest MG atlas to date (237,661 cells), we identified a tolerance checkpoint swap in MG pathogenesis. Pathological class-switched B cells within thymic germinal
papers.summary: This study generates a large single-cell and spatial transcriptomics atlas of the myasthenia gravis thymus, revealing that pathological class-switched B cells bypass canonical tolerance checkpoints and become dependent on BAFF for survival. The findings provide a new mechanistic understanding of how autoreactive B cells persist in the thymus, which may explain the inconsistent benefits of thymectomy and the poor correlation between autoantibody titers and disease severity.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics in Plants: From Cellular Maps to Mechanistic Insight.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has transformed plant biology by restoring the spatial context lost in bulk and dissociation-based transcriptomic approaches. This review synthesizes recent progress across diverse plant species and tissues, showing that gene expression is not only cell-type specific but also tightly organized by position within organs and developmental niches. Studies of meristems, vascular tissues, and floral organs reveal spatially segregated developmental programs underlying growth and differentiation; seed and grain analyses uncover compartmentalized programs controlling nutrient t
papers.summary: This review highlights how spatial transcriptomics is transforming plant biology by revealing that gene expression is organized by position within organs and developmental niches, not just by cell type. It synthesizes recent findings across meristems, vascular tissues, floral organs, and seeds, showing how spatially segregated programs control growth, differentiation, and nutrient allocation.

papers.title: Decoding macrophage-driven tumor heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma using spatial and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Macrophages play critical roles in tumorigenesis and progression; however, their functions in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we leveraged multiple perspectives, including bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics, to conduct an integrated analysis of various databases. We identified two macrophage-associated gene signatures, SLC11A1 and IFI30, and established a classifier based on these genes that correlates with different RCC prognoses and molecular patterns. This classifier significantly predicts
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). The authors identify two macrophage-associated gene signatures (SLC11A1 and IFI30) and build a prognostic classifier that correlates with distinct RCC molecular patterns and patient outcomes.

papers.title: Integrated inference of cellular compositions and gene expression programs by deconvolution.
papers.abstract: While computational deconvolution is routinely used to estimate cell-type proportions from tissue mixtures, reconstructing cell-type-specific transcriptomes at single-sample resolution remains a fundamentally underdetermined algorithmic challenge. Consequently, accurate single-sample, gene-level inference is rarely achieved by existing tools. Here, we systematically benchmarked multiple deconvolution approaches across diverse biological contexts using both pseudo-bulk mixtures and real bulk RNA-seq datasets derived from multiple tissues. Evaluating the critical computational limitations in the
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational deconvolution methods for estimating cell-type proportions and reconstructing cell-type-specific gene expression from bulk RNA-seq data. It identifies key limitations in achieving accurate single-sample, gene-level inference and evaluates performance across diverse tissues and pseudo-bulk mixtures.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors. It identifies specific microbial taxa and inflammatory mediators that may influence tumor risk, highlighting the gut-immune-brain axis as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: An Explanatory Deep Learning Pipeline for the Prediction and Visualization of Spatially Resolved Biomarker Expression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Histopathologic evaluation remains central to cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, yet the molecular programs underlying distinct tissue morphologies aren't routinely accessible in clinical workflows. Spatial transcriptomic/proteomic platforms provide region-specific molecular measurements but are limited by cost, throughput, and scalability. Most computational pathology models rely on either bulk tissue-based gene expression or a focused gene/protein expression-panel prediction, thereby obscuring subregion-specific morpho-molecular relationships and limiting spatial interpretation of a wi
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning pipeline that predicts spatially resolved biomarker expression directly from histopathology images in triple-negative breast cancer, enabling visualization of subregion-specific molecular patterns without costly spatial assays. The approach addresses limitations of existing computational pathology models by providing spatial interpretation of gene/protein expression from routine H&E slides.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes in Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF binding motifs relate to transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility, filling a gap in existing genomic analysis tools.

papers.title: Sample Preparation for Imaging-Based Spatial Transcriptomics in Rigid Plant Tissues (Roots, Shoots).
papers.abstract: Plant roots dynamically respond to environmental changes and serve as an ideal system for studying cell development and gene regulation. Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution mapping of gene expression while preserving spatial context. However, existing sample preparation techniques remain inadequate for handling rigid plant tissues such as crop roots. Here, we present a detailed and practical protocol for preparing rigid plant tissue samples for imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. The workflow ensures effective tissue handling while maintaini
papers.summary: This protocol provides a detailed workflow for preparing rigid plant tissues, such as crop roots, for imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, addressing a key gap in sample preparation. It enables high-resolution gene expression mapping while preserving spatial context, which is critical for studying plant development and environmental responses.

papers.title: Uncovering ectopic GC-like niches for tumor reactive lymphocyte priming in lung adenocarcinoma using Stereo-XCR-seq.
papers.abstract: T/B cell receptors (T/BCR), coordinating antigen-targeting immune response, play crucial roles in anti-tumor immune response. Tracking T and B cell clonal evolution in situ at single-cell resolution is essential for understanding the adaptive immune responses. To address the lack of tools for in situ single-cell T/BCR (XCR) sequencing, we develop Stereo-XCR-seq, an efficient method for retrieving and sequencing TCR and BCR from spatial transcriptome cDNA libraries at subcellular resolution. Stereo-XCR-seq enables high-fidelity, unbiased recovery of XCR sequences alongside spatial transcriptomi
papers.summary: The authors developed Stereo-XCR-seq, a method that retrieves T and B cell receptor sequences from spatial transcriptomics libraries at subcellular resolution. Applying it to lung adenocarcinoma, they identified ectopic germinal center-like niches where tumor-reactive lymphocytes are primed, providing new insights into in situ adaptive immune responses.

papers.title: EGFR inhibition promotes functional engraftment and graft survival via donor-derived CHI3L1 in fetal RPE suspension transplantation.
papers.abstract: Numerous clinical trials have highlighted the translational potential of retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cell transplantation in retinal degeneration (RD). However, an unsolved challenge remains in addressing chronic graft dysfunction, primarily due to poor integration and cell loss. Here, we perform a single-cell transcriptomic comparison between grafted RPE cells and host RPE. Our analysis identifies EGFR expression in donor fetal RPE cells as a significant obstacle to functional integration. Through multimodal imaging and spatial transcriptomics, we demonstrate that EGFR inhibition (EGFRi)
papers.summary: This study identifies EGFR expression in donor fetal retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells as a key barrier to successful integration and survival after transplantation. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, the authors show that EGFR inhibition promotes functional engraftment and graft survival, partly through donor-derived CHI3L1 signaling, offering a potential strategy to improve RPE transplantation outcomes in retinal degeneration.

papers.title: Lineage-calibrated peripheral monocyte-derived myeloid states in neurodegenerative disease: Recruitment, lesion decoding, and state persistence.
papers.abstract: Peripheral monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages are increasingly implicated in neurodegenerative disease, yet interpretation remains limited by phenotypic convergence with resident microglia, inconsistent lineage attribution, and strong dependence on experimental model and disease stage. We present a structured, lineage-calibrated framework that separates three linked processes: a recruitment gate controlling access to CNS borders and lesions; a lesion-decoding hub through which aggregate, lipid, cytokine, complement, antigenic, hypoxic, and danger-associated inputs are interpreted; and
papers.summary: This paper presents a structured framework for understanding how peripheral monocytes contribute to neurodegenerative disease, distinguishing them from resident microglia and clarifying their roles in recruitment, lesion response, and persistence. It provides a lineage-calibrated approach that could improve interpretation of myeloid cell states across disease stages and models.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method for annotating cell types in single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs) into a heterogeneous graph learning framework. It iteratively refines cell type predictions using regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, improving annotation accuracy over existing methods that ignore this information.

papers.title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) dynamically orchestrate cell fate emergence remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present GRNvelo, a computational framework that reconstructs multiscale cell fate dynamics by integrating GRNs with phenotypic dynamics from temporal single-cell RNA-seq data. GRNvelo establishes a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous multiscale model that couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with nonlocal cell growth-mediated population dynamics. To operationalize this model, GRNvelo devises a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm
papers.summary: GRNvelo is a new computational framework that integrates gene regulatory networks with temporal single-cell RNA-seq data to reconstruct multiscale cell fate dynamics. It couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with population-level growth dynamics using a two-phase optimization algorithm, providing a biologically interpretable model of how gene networks orchestrate cell fate emergence.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper reports a rapid, ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a new in vitro model for studying human ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. Single-cell RNA-sequencing confirmed the expression of developmental lineage markers and steroidogenic pathway genes in the differentiated cells.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals the Potential of ZDHHC16 in Tumor Progression and Immune Regulation.
papers.abstract: S-palmitoylation is a crucial post-translational modification that regulates diverse cellular processes, particularly signalling pathways. The ZDHHC family of enzymes catalyzes this modification, however, the role of ZDHHC16 in cancer warrants in-depth investigation. This study presents a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of ZDHHC16, examining its expression patterns, clinical relevance, associations with immune responses, genomic characteristics, and potential as a therapeutic target. We further analysed single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to identify specific cell populations associa
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of ZDHHC16, a palmitoyltransferase enzyme, revealing its expression patterns, clinical relevance, and associations with immune responses across multiple cancer types. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify specific cell populations linked to ZDHHC16, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target in tumor progression and immune regulation.

papers.title: AddaGCN: Spatial transcriptomics deconvolution using graph convolutional networks with adversarial discriminative domain adaptation.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics has substantially improved our understanding of the spatial architecture and gene expression heterogeneity within tissues. However, many spatial transcriptomics techniques can not reach single-cell resolution, instead measuring gene expression profiles from mixtures of potentially heterogeneous cell types. Here we propose AddaGCN, a robust deconvolution method to infer cell type composition from spatial transcriptomic data. AddaGCN leverages graph convolutional networks to incorporate spatial information and adopts an adversarial discriminative
papers.summary: AddaGCN is a new computational method that uses graph convolutional networks and adversarial domain adaptation to infer cell type composition from spatial transcriptomics data, improving deconvolution accuracy by incorporating spatial information. The approach addresses the challenge of mixed gene expression profiles in spatial transcriptomics, offering a robust tool for studying tissue heterogeneity.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS). The findings reveal common molecular signatures that may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and provide insights into the shared pathophysiology of these conditions.

papers.title: T cell antigenic recognition sequencing (TAR-seq) enables precise characterization of vaccine-elicited cellular immunity ex vivo and in vivo.
papers.abstract: The functional responses of antigen (Ag) specific T cells are complex, clonotype-specific, context-dependent, and incompletely captured by dominant analytic approaches. Here we present T Cell Antigenic Recognition Sequencing (TAR-seq), a two-part process that uses single-cell RNA + T cell receptor sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) to provide a precise and comprehensive characterization of the differentiation state and functional response of T cells specific to a given antigen, ex vivo and in vivo.
papers.summary: TAR-seq is a new two-part method that combines single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing to precisely characterize the differentiation state and functional response of antigen-specific T cells. It enables comprehensive analysis of vaccine-elicited cellular immunity both ex vivo and in vivo, capturing clonotype-specific and context-dependent responses that are missed by dominant approaches.

papers.title: Spatial immune programs associated with nodal status differ between lymphoid follicular regions and peritumoral tonsillar tissue in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer.
papers.abstract: In human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), lymph node metastasis is common, yet its biological and prognostic implications remain incompletely understood. Less is known about the spatial organization of immune programs within tumor-associated secondary lymphoid structures.
papers.summary: This study maps the spatial organization of immune cells in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, revealing that immune programs differ between lymphoid follicular regions and peritumoral tonsillar tissue depending on lymph node status. The findings suggest that nodal metastasis is associated with distinct local immune microenvironments, which may have prognostic relevance.

papers.title: TGFBI in tumors and the tumor immune microenvironment: functional roles, mechanisms, and therapeutic targeting.
papers.abstract: TGFBI in tumors, providing a comprehensive theoretical foundation for developing TGFBI-based precision diagnosis and treatment. Transforming growth factor-beta-induced protein (TGFBI) is a secreted extracellular matrix protein involved in various physiological and pathological processes. Its multiple roles in tumorigenesis and the remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) have recently drawn increasing attention. This review systematically compares the dual pro-tumor and tumor-suppressive functions of TGFBI across multiple cancer types and provides a comprehensive analysis of its
papers.summary: This review systematically examines the dual roles of TGFBI in cancer, highlighting its context-dependent pro-tumor and tumor-suppressive functions across different cancer types and its impact on the tumor immune microenvironment. It provides a comprehensive theoretical foundation for developing TGFBI-based precision diagnostics and therapies.

papers.title: Targeted therapy against recurrent anti-synthetase syndrome associated interstitial lung disease after bilateral lung transplantation guided by transcriptomic analyses: a case-based study.
papers.abstract: Anti-synthetase syndrome (ASS) associated interstitial lung disease (ILD) usually responds to immunosuppressive therapy, but recurrence is common. We report a 58-year-old man with ASS-ILD who developed recurrent ILD within one year after bilateral lung transplantation (LTx). Despite triple immunosuppression (glucocorticoids, tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil), systemic inflammation persisted. This case represents an in vivo model of ASS-ILD recurrence, warranting further investigation into underlying mechanisms and novel therapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This case study describes a patient with anti-synthetase syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease who experienced disease recurrence after lung transplantation despite standard immunosuppression. Transcriptomic analysis guided targeted therapy, offering insights into the mechanisms of recurrence and potential treatment strategies.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify TRIP6 as a prognostic and EMT-associated biomarker in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound molecular heterogeneity and complex tumor-microenvironment interactions, which contribute to invasion, metastasis, and variable clinical outcomes. More effective prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets are still needed.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify TRIP6 as a potential prognostic biomarker in colorectal cancer, linking its expression to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings suggest TRIP6 could serve as a therapeutic target, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Targeting regulatory T cell plasticity in gastric cancer: a unified bimodal model and precision immunotherapy paradigm: a hypothesis-generating review.
papers.abstract: In contrast to other solid tumors, gastric cancer exhibits a particularly high dependence on regulatory T cell (Treg)-mediated immunosuppression. This reliance represents a critical driver of both primary and acquired resistance to programmed death-1/ligand-1(PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors. By integrating existing single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and clinical evidence, this review proposes a unified bimodal model of the Treg tumor microenvironment. Within this framework, the immune status in gastric cancer is determined by the dynamic equilibrium between immunosuppressive stable-type Tregs and pro
papers.summary: This review proposes a unified bimodal model of regulatory T cell (Treg) plasticity in gastric cancer, integrating single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and clinical evidence to explain resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. It suggests that the balance between immunosuppressive stable-type Tregs and pro-inflammatory Tregs determines immune status, and outlines a precision immunotherapy paradigm targeting this plasticity.

papers.title: CENPM as a biomarker and therapeutic target for lymph node metastasis in thyroid carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is a key prognostic determinant in thyroid carcinoma (THCA), yet molecular markers capturing intrinsic metastatic potential are limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies CENPM as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for lymph node metastasis in thyroid carcinoma, based on bioinformatics analysis and validation. The findings suggest that CENPM expression correlates with metastatic potential and could serve as a prognostic marker or drug target.

papers.title: Spatially localized immune metaprograms reveal micro-niche organization in the human Dorsal Root Ganglion.
papers.abstract: Dorsal root ganglion (DRG)-targeted local interventions are widely used in pain management; however, the cellular and spatial organization of immune transcriptional states within human DRG tissue remains poorly defined. In particular, it is unclear whether DRG immune activity reflects a single dominant inflammatory axis or a spatially heterogeneous microenvironment composed of parallel transcriptional programs. To address this question, we analyzed publicly available human DRG single-nucleus RNA sequencing data (GSE189501) to identify immune transcriptional metaprograms using rank-stable non-n
papers.summary: This study analyzes publicly available human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) single-nucleus RNA sequencing data to identify immune transcriptional metaprograms, revealing that immune activity in the DRG is not a single dominant inflammatory axis but rather a spatially heterogeneous microenvironment composed of parallel transcriptional programs. The findings suggest that DRG immune responses are organized into distinct micro-niches, which could inform targeted pain management interventions.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals an SPP1-centered immune-fibrotic axis associated with fibrosis-related tissue remodeling in IgG4-related disease.
papers.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a fibroinflammatory condition characterized by progressive organ damage; however, the spatial organization linking immune dysregulation to fibrotic remodeling remains incompletely understood. In this study, we performed spatial transcriptomic analysis of submandibular gland tissues from patients with IgG4-RD representing two distinct fibrosis-associated tissue states. Gene expression data were normalized and z-scored, and immune- and fibrosis-related module scores were calculated. Fibrotic niches were defined based on COL1A1 expression and fibroblast signature
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular organization of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) in submandibular gland tissues, revealing an SPP1-centered immune-fibrotic axis that links immune dysregulation with fibrotic tissue remodeling. By defining fibrotic niches based on COL1A1 expression and fibroblast signatures, the authors identify distinct tissue states and potential drivers of fibrosis in IgG4-RD.

papers.title: Divergent cytotoxic and inflammatory functions of intratumoral Vδ2+ γδ T cells in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells are blood-circulating, innate-like lymphocytes that contribute to tumor immunosurveillance and constitute over 95% of Vδ2+ γδ T cells, but how they perform antitumor or protumor functions remains unclear. Here, we comprehensively characterized Vδ2+ γδ T cells in paired peripheral blood and tumor samples from patients with renal cell carcinoma using flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomic analysis. We identified two major Vδ2+ γδ T cell subsets distinguished by expression of CD16, which were present at variable proportions in both circulation and tumors. Notably, the propor
papers.summary: This study characterizes Vδ2+ γδ T cells in renal cell carcinoma patients, identifying two major subsets defined by CD16 expression that have divergent cytotoxic and inflammatory functions within tumors. Using flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics, the authors reveal how these subsets may contribute to either antitumor or protumor activities, providing insights into their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis of kidney biopsies identifies activation of complement and SPP1 networks in Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis (SAGN) has emerged as the leading cause of infection-related glomerulonephritis (IRGN) in the Western subcontinents, but pathogenesis remains poorly understood in the absence of animal models and detailed molecular mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics on kidney biopsies from patients with Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis (SAGN) to identify key molecular pathways, revealing activation of complement and SPP1 networks. These findings provide new insights into the pathogenesis of SAGN, which lacks animal models, and highlight potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: sNucConv: A bulk RNA-seq deconvolution method trained on single-nucleus RNA-seq data to estimate cell-type composition of human adipose tissues
papers.abstract: Summary Deconvolution algorithms mostly rely on single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data applied onto bulk RNA-sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) to estimate tissues’ cell-type composition, with performance accuracy validated on deposited databases. Adipose tissues’ cellular composition is highly variable, and adipocytes can only be captured by single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq). Here we report the development of sNucConv, a Scaden deep-learning-based deconvolution tool, trained using 5 hSAT and 7 hVAT snRNA-seq-based data corrected by (i) snRNA-seq/bulk RNA-seq highly correlated genes and (i
papers.summary: sNucConv is a new deep-learning deconvolution tool that uses single-nucleus RNA-seq data from human adipose tissues to estimate cell-type composition from bulk RNA-seq, addressing the challenge that adipocytes are only captured by snRNA-seq. The method improves accuracy by training on snRNA-seq data corrected with highly correlated genes between snRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq, providing a more reliable way to study adipose tissue heterogeneity.
